lines.text: You've probably been told that swallowed gum sits inside your stomach for seven years.
The truth is, that is completely false.
While your stomach acid can't dissolve the rubbery synthetic gum base, your body breaks down everything else.
Powerful muscular contractions called peristalsis push the gum through your intestines.
Within forty-eight hours, the gum passes out in the toilet completely harmlessly.
However, swallowing huge clumps of gum at once can form a dangerous digestive blockage called a bezoar.
So while an accidental swallow won't hurt, it's always best to spit it out.
